title: Deployment Certification: Security Governance Playbook
author: Marina Ortega
summary: A cross-functional playbook describing the security gates and evidence requirements for certifying a deployment (hosted, dedicated, or private). Covers RBAC, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC checkpoints, incident response expectations for certified deployments, and the risk & exception approval workflow.
body:
Overview

This playbook defines the security governance controls and the certification workflow required before a Redwood deployment is promoted to an externally-facing or production tier. It combines technical controls (RBAC, logging, data residency), process gates (SDLC checklists), and evidence packaging for audits. The goal is to provide a repeatable, auditable path that balances operational velocity with compliance assurance.

Scope

- Applies to: Hosted API services, Dedicated clusters, Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments, and associated control plane components.
- Excludes: Experimental prototypes in personal sandboxes (see sandbox exceptions process).

Principles

1. Principle of least privilege: role definitions must be narrowly scoped and assigned via group membership.
2. Evidence-first certification: every deployment must publish a certification bundle before go-live.
3. Observable by default: audit logs, metrics, and traces necessary for post-incident analysis must be enabled.
4. Residency-aware configuration: deployment configuration must express data residency and retention settings as part of the manifest.

Owners & Roles

- Security (owner): governance, final certification, exception approvals for risk > medium.
- Eng-Platform: implement RBAC plumbing, maintain logging collectors, and validation scripts.
- Eng-SRE: operational readiness, runbooks, and uptime SLOs.
- Product/Customer Success: validate customer requirements for dedicated/private deployments.
- Compliance: coordinates evidence for audits and regulatory requests.

High-level Certification Checklist (must-pass items)

1) RBAC & Authentication
- Role matrix: documented mapping of roles -> permissions -> scoping (namespace/tenant).
- Admin separation: at least two distinct admin roles (operator-admin, security-admin) with dual approval for elevation.
- MFA enforced for all interactive accounts; service-to-service uses short-lived mTLS or signed JWTs.
- Approval: automated policy check (CI gate) verifying no wildcard privileges present.

2) Audit Logging
- Ingestion: All auth decisions, privilege changes, and sensitive API calls must be emitted to the central audit topic.
- Tamper-evidence: logs are immutably stored (WORM or object-store immutability policy) and checksummed.
- Retention mapping: retention time must be explicitly mapped to data residency needs and regulatory requirements (table below).
- Alerting: anomalous access patterns generate alerts to sec-ops on a 24/7 channel.

3) Data Residency & Retention
- Residency statement: the deployment manifest must include a data_residency field (region code) and a retention_policy reference.
- Personal data: PII/PHI-specific retention rules enforced by data classification service.
- Cross-border flow: any cross-region replication requires documented legal basis and DSAR handling plan.

4) Secure SDLC Gates
- Static analysis: PRs must pass SAST and dependency vulnerability scans before merge.
- SBOM: an SBOM artifact must be attached to release artifacts and included in the certification bundle.
- Secret scanning: CI must reject releases with high/critical secrets detected.
- Infra-as-code: IaC templates validated against org security policies (policy-as-code).

5) Incident Response & Forensics
- Preservation: deployment must support immediate snapshot of audit logs, persistent volumes, and network flow logs on suspected compromise.
- Contacts: dedicated incident contacts must be included in the certification bundle with escalation matrix.
- Playbooks: a tailored runbook for the service (triage, containment, evidence capture) must exist and be current within 90 days.

Certification Evidence Bundle (required artifacts)

- Role matrix CSV (roles, group ids, permissions)
- Audit-log retention mapping (CSV/JSON) and sample query proving log ingestion
- Deployment manifest (including data_residency, retention_policy reference)
- SBOM and dependency-scan report
- CI/CD pipeline gate logs (SAST, secret-scan pass/fail)
- Incident runbook and on-call roster snapshot
- Signed attestation from Eng-Platform and Security (PDF)

Example artifact table (human-readable)

| Artifact | Required format | Owner | Freshness | Notes |
|---------|----------------|-------|----------|-------|
| Role matrix | CSV | Eng-Platform | within 30d | Must reference central directory group IDs |
| Audit mapping | JSON/CSV | Security | within 90d | Show retention per log class and region |
| SBOM | SPDX or CycloneDX | Eng-Dev | per release | Attach to release tag |
| Runbook | Markdown/Confluence | Eng-SRE | within 90d | Include evidence collection commands |

Detailed Procedures

A. CI Certification Gate (automated)
1. Developer opens a release PR and attaches the deployment manifest.
2. CI runs policy-as-code checks (RBAC lint, IaC security, dependency checks).
3. If any high-severity failure: PR blocked and automated ticket created for remediation.
4. On success: CI produces a certification artifact (cert.json) with checksums and attaches to the release.

B. Manual Review & Attestation (human)
1. Submission: Eng-Platform or service owner requests certification by uploading evidence bundle to the Certification Jira project.
2. Security review: Security runs the checklist, verifies logs, and requests remediation for gaps.
3. Dual attestation: Security and Eng-Platform leads sign the attestation PDF; Compliance may co-sign for regulated workloads.
4. Post-approval: SRE enables the production routing flag and notifies Product.

C. Incident-triggered Re-certification
1. Any Sev-2+ incident that impacts control efficacy triggers a forced re-certification.
2. Rerun automated CI checks against release tag and re-upload updated evidence.
3. Security performs a focused review; any unresolved medium/high findings block traffic resumption.

RBAC policy example (YAML - illustrative)

roles:
  - name: service-reader
    description: Read-only access to service resources in tenant namespace
    permissions:
      - resources: ["/v1/requests", "/v1/metrics"]
        verbs: ["get","list"]
    scope: "tenant:${TENANT_ID}"

  - name: operator-admin
    description: Operational admin for node & infra operations
    permissions:
      - resources: ["/infra/*", "/nodes/*"]
        verbs: ["create","update","delete","get"]
    approval: "2-person"

Audit retention mapping (example JSON snippet - for reviewer use)

{
  "auth_events": {"retention_days": 1095, "region": "eu-west-1"},
  "access_control_changes": {"retention_days": 1825, "region": "us-west-2"},
  "infra_metrics": {"retention_days": 365, "region": "global"}
}

(Production artifact must be stored as CSV/JSON in the evidence repo; snippet above is illustrative only.)

Data Residency Decision Matrix (summary)

- If customer data is regulated (GDPR, CCPA, data-protection addendum) -> deploy to customer-specified region only.
- If non-PII operational telemetry only -> default multi-region replication with aggregated retention policy.
- If on-prem required -> ensure control plane meets customer KMS/HSM requirements and sign-off from Compliance.

Risk & Exception Workflow

1) Low risk (config-level): Service owner raises an Access Exception ticket with compensating control description; reviewer: Security team single approver; TTL <= 30 days.
2) Medium risk (process-level): Requires Security + Eng-Platform approval and a mitigating plan with milestones; TTL <= 90 days with mandatory quarterly attestations.
3) High risk (design-level): Requires Security leadership + Compliance review + CTO sign-off; must include compensating technical controls and an emergency rollback plan.

Exception request template (required fields)

- Service name
- Owner
- Risk classification (low/medium/high)
- Description and rationale
- Proposed compensating controls
- Expiry date
- Evidence of customer notification (if applicable)

Operational tooling & automation

- Certification registry: an internal service that stores certification artifacts and exposes an API to check certification status. Eng-Platform owns the service.
- Automated validators: set of containerized checks that validate RBAC matrices, sampling log ingestion, and SBOM presence. These run in CI and in pre-flight checks.
- Evidence collector: lightweight CLI to assemble evidence bundle: 
  - run: redwood-evidence collect --service my-service --release v1.2.3 --out bundle.zip

Audit & Review cadence

- Continuous: automated CI checks run on every release.
- Quarterly: Security performs spot audits of certified deployments chosen via risk-based sampling.
- Annual: Full recertification for regulated workloads (PCI/ISO/SOC scoped services).

Common failure modes & remediations

- Missing audit streams: remediate by deploying the logging sidecar and re-validating ingestion.
- Over-privileged role granted in IaC: revoke, issue a patch PR with least-privilege fix, and rerun CI gate.
- Unsupported region replication: if legal review disallows cross-border replication, disable replication and notify affected customers; run re-certification.

Appendix: Useful commands and queries

1) Verify audit ingestion (example):
$ kafka-console-consumer --bootstrap-server audit.example:9092 --topic auth-events --from-beginning --max-messages 1

2) Collect evidence (example):
$ redwood-evidence collect --service search-api --release v2026-01-18 --out /tmp/search-evidence.zip

3) Query retention mapping (example SQL):
SELECT log_class, retention_days, region FROM compliance.audit_retention WHERE service = 'search-api';
